statement: Nzinga a Nkuwu, ruler of Kongo, was baptized 3 May 1491 by Portuguese missionaries, taking the name João I; his son Nzinga a Mbemba (later Afonso I) and court officials were baptized alongside him. João I abandoned Christianity c. 1494-95, reportedly in significant part because Catholic monogamy requirements conflicted with the polygynous marriage-alliance politics central to Kongo's elective/matrilineal succession system — this specific causal claim is reported across secondary sources but was not traced to one named peer-reviewed primary citation in this research pass.

sources.citation: General secondary historiography on the 1491 Kongo royal baptism and João I's apostasy.

notes: Flagged for follow-up verification against Thornton directly or Anne Hilton, The Kingdom of Kongo (Oxford UP, 1985).
